small_guidance:
- The current kernel recomputes the conv 16× per output (once per pool-element dh,dw) instead of once. Restructure so each (kh,kw,ic) load contributes to all POOL*POOL pre-pool positions, or better, compute the OH×OW conv tile once and then average-pool — this alone should cut work by ~16×.
- Add `triton.autotune` over BLOCK_PH ∈ {4,8,16}, BLOCK_PW ∈ {16,32,64}, num_warps ∈ {4,8}, num_stages ∈ {2,3}; with PH=PW=95 a 16×32 tile better amortizes weight loads.
- Cache the OC×IC×KH×KW weight tile in registers (static_range over IC,KH,KW already done) but hoist `tl.load(w_ptr+...)` outside the dh,dw loop so weights are loaded once per program, not 16×.
large_guidance:
- Redesign as an implicit-GEMM conv: one program per (N, OC-tile, pooled-spatial-tile). For each pooled output (ph,pw), accumulate the full POOL×POOL conv window directly into a single scalar per (oc, ph, pw) — i.e., sum_{dh,dw,ic,kh,kw} x[..]*w[..] in one fused loop nest, divide by POOL², sigmoid, then reduce across OC and (ph,pw) into a per-N partial via atomic_add. This avoids materializing the BLOCK_PH×BLOCK_PW conv tile 16 times.
- Switch the reduction strategy: since the final output is just N scalars, make OC the inner reduction axis of each program (one program per (N, pooled-tile), looping OC inside) so the sigmoid+sum-over-OC happens in registers without any atomics across OC — only one atomic_add per (N, pooled-tile) into out[n].
- Consider channels_last input layout (NHWC) so the IC loop becomes a contiguous vector load of width IC=8, enabling `tl.dot`-style MMA on the (BLOCK_PH*BLOCK_PW, IC) × (IC, OC) inner product; with IC=8 and OC=64 this maps cleanly to a small GEMM tile.
